title: HPOQuest: A Rare-Disease Diagnostic Agent Using Active Phenotype Acquisition
authors: Kamilia Zaripova, Nassir Navab et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: More than 300 million people worldwide are affected by one of over 7,000 known rare diseases, yet diagnosis remains difficult because patients initially present with incomplete and heterogeneous phenotypes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present HPOQuest, a training-free framework for sequential phenotype acquisition in rare-disease diagnosis. Starting from a small set of observed patient phenotypes, HPOQuest maintains a probabilistic disease ranking and iteratively selects informative follow-up questions to support clinicians during patient assessment.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Confirmed phenotypes update the disease ranking, while all responses update the candidate question set. Across four benchmark cohorts, HPOQuest substantially improves diagnosis from sparse initial phenotypes, with gains of up to 30% points at Recall@1 and 45% points at Recall@5.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that sequential phenotype acquisition can substantially improve rare-disease diagnosis from limited initial clinical evidence.

slides.hook: Exoskeletons have shown great potential for augmenting human physical capabilities, yet generating reliable assistance remains challenging because human motion patterns and interaction requirements vary substantially in practice.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To address this problem, a dual-loop assistance strategy is proposed to couple multimodal exoskeleton trajectory generation with variable admittance control, where trajectory variance links the outer-loop generator and the inner-loop controller. In the inner loop, multiple future trajectories are sampled from the generator to estimate the trajectory mean and variance.

slides.hook: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) often act against multiple pathogen classes, making multi-label activity prediction a more realistic screening target than binary antimicrobial classification.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The ESCAPE benchmark formalizes this setting, but leading approaches typically rely on multimodal, structure-conditioned deep models that are costly to train and tune. We show that a simple, sequence-only pipeline can match and surpass these methods by combining 330 interpretable sequence descriptors with TabPFN, a tabular foundation model that performs in-context prediction in a single forward pass without gradient-based training or hyperparameter search.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On ESCAPE (82,359 peptides; five labels), a label-powerset TabPFN model achieves mAP-5 = 77.8%, improving on the previously best reported 72.1%. A probabilistic classifier chain is the first method to match or exceed the best published average precision on each of the five labels simultaneously.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: A Reality Check of Inference-Time Context Augmentation Methods
authors: Haeun Yu, Geert Heyman et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) often fail to utilise the context given in the input, resulting in hallucinations or a fallback to parametric knowledge.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Context augmentation methods aim to improve model performance by modifying the input, from inserting filler tokens that add computational time to adding relevant content such as elaboration of a context during inference. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this paper, we present an evaluation framework spanning five methods that differ in how informative the inserted content is and apply them at the sentence level across seven models spanning multiple sizes on three datasets. We find that accuracy gains are not always genuine improvements but undirected perturbations: the methods correct some predictions while breaking others, particularly when the inserted text allows only for more computational time.

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) serve users whose cultural identities are multi-layered, yet cultural evaluations commonly reduce identity to one label.

slides.content: In this work, we study LLMs under simultaneous identity cues, with a country persona in the system prompt and a second identity signaled in the user turn, either by naming a country (explicit cue) or through the query language (implicit cue). slides.hook: Synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data generation offers a promising route for privacy-aware biomedical data sharing, but donor-linked datasets require careful balancing of biological utility and privacy risk.

title: OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies

slides.hook: Sparse attention reads only a small subset of the key-value cache, and how to treat the unread tail remains a key challenge.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Discarding the tail biases the output, and sampling it as previous approaches do fails at reads of 5% and below, where the tail likely holds heavy hitters the selector missed. Our key observation is that the simplest possible proxy, one token that folds the entire tail into its count-aware mean, already yields lower output error than a sample at every read behind a practical selector.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We further show in closed form that at low reads sampling nearly doubles the weight error of discarding while a single proxy stays below it. Building on these findings, we explore approximating the dense attention distribution with a few proxies that target the tail.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: Multimodal reasoning for broadly neutralizing antibody discovery from label-free human B cell repertoires across virus families
authors: Hantao Lou, Jianqing Zheng et al. (24 researchers)

slides.hook: Discovering broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) from human natural immune repertoires remains a fundamental challenge in immunology, hindered by: the extreme rarity of bnAb, incomplete understanding of their cellular origins across pathogens, and the inability of existing computational tools to generalize across emerging viral threats.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we present ImmuneAgent, a closed-loop AI system that integrates multimodal reasoning with continual meta-learning and wet-lab feedback to overcome these barriers. Applied to screen the natural BCR repertoires from vaccinated or infected cohorts, the system achieves a ~55% neutralization antibody discovery rate (60 of 110 cloned candidates) and a ~11% bnAb yield (12 of 110), substantially outperforming a state-of-the-art sequence-based neutralization predictor or cofolding models evaluated at the same cloning budget.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Five ImmuneAgent-discovered antibodies conferred 100% in vivo protection against lethal influenza challenge, comparable to the clinical-stage therapeutic MEDI8852. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results validate that ImmuneAgent is a generalizable framework for rapid therapeutic antibody discovery against emerging viral threats.

slides.hook: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in f-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds.

title: Binder migration across film consolidation and pore emptying in electrode drying: a continuous model validated against drying-rate, thickness, and schedule experiments
authors: Younghwan Joo, Sanghyun Oh et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Drying battery electrodes faster saves energy but drives dissolved binder toward the film surface, depleting the current-collector interface and weakening adhesion.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Models of this migration stop convecting the binder when film consolidation ends, and models of the subsequent pore emptying omit the binder or start from an assumed binder field, so no simulation has followed binder convection through both stages that a drying schedule acts on. This study presents a continuous simulation of the dissolved binder field across both stages, driven by the published drying rates and completed by effective descriptions of the two questions the base transport physics leaves open: where the liquid of the consolidating film carries the binder, and when the binder stops moving as the pores empty.

title: Stellar Loci X: Selection of Nitrogen-Rich Giants Using GALEX NUV and Synthetic SDSS Photometry
authors: Liangyu Yu, Haibo Yuan et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Nitrogen-rich (N-rich) field stars (likely second-generation escapees from globular clusters) provide a powerful, but currently sample-limited, probe of globular-cluster disruption in the Galactic halo.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We exploit the fact that enhanced NH, CN absorption depresses optical u band flux, while the near-ultraviolet (NUV) band is largely insensitive to nitrogen enhancement while remaining sensitive to overall metallicity. title: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning
authors: Junyu Lin, Bosong Qi et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Real-world deployment of personalized federated learning (PFL) requires adapting to heterogeneous clients while preserving recognition performance beyond local distributions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, high local accuracy can conceal failures on locally rare or absent classes. Effective personalization should therefore strengthen global recognition while raising the personalization floor.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We propose an evaluation protocol that complements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations to reveal generalization obscured by local scores, and assesses personalization floors among the worst-performing clients to expose weaknesses hidden by aggregate performance. To meet these deployment challenges, we propose FedGRC, a unified PFL framework integrating generalization and personalization through (i) Consensus-Guided Representation Learning (CGRL), which learns discriminative representations through shared directional and magnitude guidance; (ii) Multilayer Metric Synthesis (MMS), which constructs a shared covariance metric from these multilayer representations for statistical classification; and (iii) Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization (SASP), which adapts class means within this metric by shrinking local estimates toward shared means according to local sample support, enabling adaptation while retaining shared knowledge.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On the real-world heterogeneous FedRS dataset, it outperforms the respective best baselines by 2.15%, 3.30%, and 4.61% in local adaptation, global recognition, and the personalization floor.

title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
authors: Chao Gu & Quanyan Zhu

slides.hook: This paper studies the problem of safe tool execution for large language model (LLM) agents under prompt injection.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using Petri nets, we formalize the execution harness between the LLM and its tools as a supervisory control problem, in which marks represent capabilities, approvals and budgets. Since a transition fires only if the marks it needs are present, an injected request whose preconditions are unmet or already spent is refused regardless of its wording.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Treating tool outcomes as uncontrollable, we enforce safety by the conventional maximally permissive supervisor, and this safety transfers to the running system under four assumptions. Moreover, to capture an agent that may propose again after a refusal, we introduce the notion of a replanning closed loop, in which each retry costs an inference call.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On an autonomous release agent, we find by synthesis that safe deployment requires a step that the supervisor can refuse after a rollout starts.

title: Distributed dual-comb spectroscopy
authors: Haowei Shi, Kartikeya Arora et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: We propose distributed dual-comb spectroscopy, a quantum-enhanced sensing architecture that simultaneously exploits spatial- and spectral-domain entanglement to improve the extraction of global spectroscopic information across broadband frequency ranges.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Our scheme consists of a network of Mach-Zehnder interferometers interrogating spatially separated samples, each driven by a classical frequency comb at the bright port. A single two-mode squeezed frequency comb is distributed through a passive beam-splitter array into K entangled combs, establishing multipartite correlations across sensors while preserving intrinsic spectral entanglement.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The protocol is compatible with both heterodyne detection and division detection, and enables parallel estimation of weighted-average absorption features over multiple frequency components. Compared with spatially separable quantum strategies requiring K independently engineered nonclassical comb sources, our approach achieves enhanced signal-to-noise performance using only a single quantum resource distributed across the network.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish a scalable route toward broadband distributed quantum spectroscopy with simultaneous spatial and spectral advantage.

slides.content: The historical maps (encompassing 1901–1930, 1931–1960, 1961–1990, and 1991–2020) are based on high-resolution, observation-based climatologies, while the future maps (encompassing 2041–2070 and 2071–2099) are based on downscaled and bias-corrected climate projections for seven shared socio-economic pathways (SSPs). title: Semantic Alignment of EEG and Text: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Decoding Imagined Speech
authors: Shahryar G. Namdari, Francesco Iacomi et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Imagined speech decoding from EEG offers a promising route toward naturalistic brain-computer interfaces.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Traditional closed-set classifiers treat semantic categories as independent labels and do not explicitly exploit relationships among linguistic intents, limiting output flexibility. We adapt a multimodal contrastive learning framework to imagined speech, aligning EEG trials with language representations in the embedding space of a frozen pretrained text encoder.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: An EEG encoder is trained with a composite objective combining semantically reweighted EEG-sentence alignment and text-prototype-based class discrimination, encouraging semantic structure while preserving separability among 39 intent categories. We evaluate the approach on the Chisco imagined speech dataset across five subjects, reporting Top-k accuracy, macro-F1, and balanced pairwise matching accuracy (2v2).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
authors: Mohammad Talaei, Mohammad Goudarzi et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Soil moisture and temperature govern plant-water availability and microbial activity, making them key indicators for evaluating land-restoration efforts on degraded landscapes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the physical and data-driven models normally used to forecast them both need information that a newly instrumented restoration site does not yet have: hydraulic parameters for the former and months of per-site training data for the latter. We evaluate TimesFM 1, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on 15-minute telemetry from 27 sensor stations across three land-management regimes (Control, Treatment, Scald) at a semi-arid restoration site, forecasting 5 cm and 30 cm soil moisture and enclosure temperature at seven lead times from 1 h to 168 h.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using gap-aware rolling-origin evaluation across sensors, we find that TimesFM beats the best rule-based statistical forecasting baselines (persistence, seasonal-naive, or 7-day climatology) by 21-76% at sub-daily lead times but loses by 6-79% beyond a day, a pattern explained by a diurnal-alignment mechanism that holds for both soil-moisture depths and temperature. A CatBoost baseline trained walk-forward on the same origins with full history and weather covariates never wins overall, and we show that its weakness is partly a cold-start effect specific to short deployments.

title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
authors: Blessing Isoyiza Adeika & Onyema Osuagwu

slides.hook: Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity.

title: Tracing Hallucinations in LLM Reasoning for UML Class Diagram Generation: An Empirical Taxonomy and Mitigation Study

title: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
authors: Tariq Mahassen, Marcin Jastrzebski et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We develop and analyze generative models based on quantum solvers of stochastic differential equations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Unlike the common approach based on layered variational quantum circuits with parameterized rotations, we parameterize the potential of a Langevin process. title: MORAD: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Objective Rewards for RNA Inverse Design
authors: Jixin Tang, Ji Guo et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We introduce MORAD, an online reinforcement learning framework for backbone-conditioned RNA diffusion models that trains a single shared policy across diverse target backbones.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Structure-conditioned RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences compatible with a target three-dimensional backbone, yet existing reinforcement learning approaches either optimize a separate policy for each target backbone or rely on offline preference optimization, leaving online post-training of a reusable backbone-conditioned model largely unexplored. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Beyond existing RL rewards that primarily target tertiary structural quality, MORAD jointly optimizes six measurements spanning tertiary geometry, base pairing, ensemble behavior, and sequence composition. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On the test set, MORAD outperforms RiboDiffusion, gRNAde, and RDesign across tertiary structural accuracy, secondary-structure pairing, and thermodynamic quality, establishing a new state of the art in structure-conditioned RNA inverse design.

title: Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models
authors: Hossein Resani & Javen Qinfeng Shi

slides.hook: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models in latent space, enabling efficient planning but leaving their states opaque.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Inside-JEPA, which places relational channels for ordered entity pairs inside the JEPA latent state and shows that an inverse-dynamics loss can ground these channels without relation labels when its head reads them, either alone or as part of the full state. On Something-Something V2, latent prediction alone performs no better than a random relation head, while inverse-dynamics supervision that recovers actions from channel changes improves relational AUROC by .065-.103 across ten settings with annotated boxes, by .081 on RH20T robot episodes with held-out tasks, and by .050-.061 across five relations using off-the-shelf detection and tracking.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: An inverse head on entity latents decodes actions more accurately but barely improves relational grounding; shuffled labels, two label-free objectives, and action labels on only 5% of the pairs also fail to ground the channels. Given an action, predicted relational changes approach the quality of observed future relations (AUROC .599 vs .621).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: For one-step relational goals, a supervised readout of the 16 channels ranks the correct action among the top five of 65 in 43% of cases, compared with 24% for prediction-only latents and 17% for a frequency prior.

slides.hook: Some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds.

exposition.heading: The Underlying Problem
exposition.body: Deciphering how hippocampal and entorhinal networks construct internal cognitive spatial maps continues to drive fundamental neuroscientific inquiry. To clarify these dynamics, Tatsuya Daikoku and Risa Kobayashi undertake a targeted inquiry titled Music Between Two Minds: Individual Signatures, Shared States, and the Emergence of Creative Interaction. Their analysis centers on a direct observation: some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown. This formulation offers a coherent framework that reconciles experimental observations with broader physical principles.

exposition.heading: The Core Mechanism
exposition.body: The experimental design incorporates rigorous control parameters to ensure systematic reproducibility. Here the researchers examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes. This setup allows the investigators to isolate governing variables with high fidelity, ensuring that the resulting signals reflect authentic physical behavior rather than experimental artifacts.

exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings
exposition.body: A systematic review of the experimental outputs reveals compelling empirical support for the formulation. Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos. This evidence establishes a robust performance ceiling that sets a new standard for future studies in this domain.

exposition.heading: Scientific Implications and Limits
exposition.body: Translating these findings into broader practical applications will depend on navigating specific physical boundaries. Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds. Future research will need to determine how these principles hold under extended operational conditions and whether the framework can be generalized to broader problems across the field.

slides.hook: Deep learning models have achieved strong performance in artificial intelligence for science, yet their black-box nature limits our understanding of how they learn scientific tasks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing methods for interpretability provide limited insight into how models organize evidence and evolve during learning. We introduce explainability from training (EFT), a model-agnostic paradigm that traces model interpretation during training to explain why models rely on specific features and how they organize these features as predictive evidence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We apply EFT to four state-of-the-art T cell receptor (TCR)-epitope prediction models, TCR-SRIM, TULIP, MixTCRpred, and NetTCR-2.2, spanning post-hoc and interpret-by-design approaches as well as transformers and CNNs. To investigate how structural information affects model explanations, we introduce a benchmark, TCR-XAI2, containing 388 unique experimentally resolved TCR-epitope structures, complemented by structures predicted using AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, TCRModel2, tFold-TCR, and OpenFold3.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Using EFT with TCR-XAI2, we demonstrate that (1) CNN and transformer models exhibit distinct learning trajectories; (2) TCR α and β evidence can conflict during learning, limiting the benefits of jointly modeling both chains, while MHC information mitigates this; and (3) real versus predicted structural data for TCR-epitope prediction exhibits distinct TCR and peptide feature preferences as well as differing trajectories of model certainty.

title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
authors: Sachin Gupta

slides.hook: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis.

title: MD-LLM-2: A Transferable Language Model of Molecular Dynamics with Physical Conditioning and Explicit Path Probabilities
authors: Mhd Hussein Murtada, Z. Faidon Brotzakis et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations model the motion of proteins between conformational states, but crossing free energy barriers and sampling multiple thermodynamic conditions remain computationally costly.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We recently introduced MD-LLM-1, which showed that language models can generate conformational trajectories at lower cost, but required a separate model for each protein and did not explicitly model thermodynamics or kinetics. title: CliffRank: A Dual-Branch Framework for Activity-Cliff Ranking Prediction
authors: Kewei Li, Rongying Zhang et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Activity-cliff ranking remains difficult because local structural changes can cause large activity differences, while high-quality data that resolve the underlying mechanisms remain limited.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To use available activity labels more effectively, we combine absolute-activity regression with ranking-consistency learning. CliffRank trains two parallel predictors with mean squared error, a thresholded listwise loss, and Pairwise Preference Consistency (PPC), which aligns relative ordering in the preference-probability space.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On three antimicrobial peptide datasets, CliffRank with ESM2-t12 achieved the highest mean Spearman correlation of 0.5393 and mean Recall@50 of 21.4, although the leading method varied across individual datasets. title: The i-frame and the s-frame: How focusing on individual-level solutions has led behavioral public policy astray
authors: Nick Chater A & George F. Loewenstein

slides.hook: An influential line of thinking in behavioral science, to which the two authors have long subscribed, is that many of society's most pressing problems can be addressed cheaply and effectively at the level of the individual, without modifying the system in which the individual operates.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We now believe this was a mistake, along with, we suspect, many colleagues in both the academic and policy communities. Results from such interventions have been disappointingly modest.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: But more importantly, they have guided many (though by no means all) behavioral scientists to frame policy problems in individual, not systemic, terms: To adopt what we call the "i-frame," rather than the "s-frame." The difference may be more consequential than i-frame advocates have realized, by deflecting attention and support away from s-frame policies. Indeed, highlighting the i-frame is a long-established objective of corporate opponents of concerted systemic action such as regulation and taxation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We argue that the most important way in which behavioral scientists can contribute to public policy is by employing their skills to develop and implement value-creating system-level change.

exposition.heading: The Underlying Problem

title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
authors: Hongcan Guo, Yian Zhao et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Hierarchical language generation separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, but its effectiveness depends on what the latent space compresses and how the discrete generator uses it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We propose Cola2, a framework that jointly studies continuous semantic compression, the balance between reconstruction and generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. exposition.heading: The Underlying Problem
exposition.body: A long-standing debate in machine learning concerns how artificial agents can learn world dynamics without requiring prohibitively large sample sizes. To clarify these dynamics, Hongcan Guo and Yian Zhao undertake a targeted inquiry titled Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation. Their analysis centers on a direct observation: hierarchical language generation separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, but its effectiveness depends on what the latent space compresses and how the discrete generator uses it. This formulation offers a coherent framework that reconciles experimental observations with broader physical principles.

exposition.heading: The Core Mechanism
exposition.body: The experimental design incorporates rigorous control parameters to ensure systematic reproducibility. The investigators propose Cola2, a framework that jointly studies continuous semantic compression, the balance between reconstruction and generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. Cola2 dynamically segments text into semantic spans, controls the compression rate through auxiliary-loss-free negative feedback, and combines reconstruction and generation supervision to learn compact, predictive latent representations. This setup allows the investigators to isolate governing variables with high fidelity, ensuring that the resulting signals reflect authentic physical behavior rather than experimental artifacts.

exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings
exposition.body: Direct observations from these benchmark trials corroborated the foundational propositions of the work. A block-causal masked diffusion decoder is trained with clean, noisy, and dropped latent conditions, while classifier-free guidance adjusts the balance between semantic reconstruction and autonomous generation. Token-prediction gradients update the encoder through the latents, whereas Flow Matching prior learning is decoupled from representation learning by stop-gradient. This evidence establishes a robust performance ceiling that sets a new standard for future studies in this domain.

Two token-level factors modulate the teacher's generation bias using codon position and organism-specific codon usage. slides.hook: Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers, must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. Here we demonstrate four L-couplers operating between two 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk R1 superconducting qubit processors.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Each L-coupler joins two Nighthawk lattice qubits through two frequency-tunable L-qubits, two RF-SQUID based "i2m" couplers, and 80 cm of superconducting aluminum coax. Each cable installs perpendicular to the processor surface, to enable denser connections, and is joined to the chip by an indium-to-indium room temperature pressure bond made after both modules were mounted.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation

slides.hook: Online Policy Distillation (OPD) often outperforms offline methods such as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) by training on trajectories sampled directly from the student.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, standard OPD trains the student to follow the teacher at every state of the trajectory, assuming that teacher guidance is always beneficial. We instead distinguish between what the teacher prefers and what actually helps the current student succeed.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We introduce Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation (AOPD), which weights teacher actions by their counterfactual advantage under the student. Teacher actions that improve the student's expected outcome are reinforced, while those that do not are downweighted.

title: Language Models Share a Readout Bottleneck in Working Memory
authors: Dongyu Gong

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) reproduce a human working-memory signature on the N-back task: performance declines as memory load N increases, and errors concentrate on lures, items that repeat the current stimulus at a neighboring but incorrect serial position.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We ask whether this shared behavioral signature reflects a shared mechanism. The literature offers two candidate accounts.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: Co-folding with a Soup of Representations
authors: Hyosoon Jang, Taewon Kim et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Co-folding models such as AlphaFold3, Protenix, ESMFold2, and OpenDDE have advanced rapidly, yet no single model consistently performs best across all biomolecular complexes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this paper, we show that their pair representations encode complementary information that can be transferred across models to improve structure prediction. We introduce SoupFold, which combines pair representations from multiple co-folding models in a common representation space and generates structures from the combined representation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Importantly, SoupFold does not retrain the co-folding models and learns only simple mappings to transfer representations across models. title: Density-split analyses of the pairwise kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
authors: Finn A. Roper, Aritra K. Gon et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: We consider the dependence of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect on the environments of foreground cosmological structures.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Standard pairwise kSZ estimators exploit the fact that galaxies below separations of sim 200,h^{-1}{rm M}_odot fall towards each other on average, yielding a negative mean pairwise kSZ signal. However, this signal is the residual from a near-cancellation between outflows from underdense regions and infall towards overdensities giving a large variance in the pairwise velocity distribution and hence a low signal-to-noise ratio for the mean kSZ signal.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This effect is especially marked at the largest scales, where the pairwise velocity distribution becomes more symmetric about zero. slides.hook: Chunking strategies for retrieval-augmented generation are almost always evaluated on a static snapshot, yet the documents underlying a knowledge base continue to change.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Because chunks are embedded independently, a boundary that moves after an edit forces unchanged text to be re-embedded. We measure this update cost on 120 pairs of adjacent Chinese and English Wikipedia revisions for three stateless chunkers (non-overlapping fixed-size, recursive paragraph-first, and content-defined chunking) under a strict byte-identical reuse rule and a frozen dense encoder.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On the 116-article common-success pool, with frozen, length-calibrated parameters, fixed-size chunking recomputes 57-68% of its full new-version embedding-input workload, recursive chunking 38-56%, and content-defined chunking 43-54% (it failed on 4 of 62 Chinese articles), while at these parameters mean evidence recall under a fixed 2048-token retrieval budget differs by less than two percentage points within either language. A cost-only parameter grid shows that the ranking of the two content-aware chunkers changes with chunk-length settings, whereas non-overlapping fixed-size chunking has the highest recomputation cost in every length-matched condition.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Update cost is therefore a substantial, parameter-sensitive dimension that static retrieval evaluations do not expose and that should be reported alongside retrieval quality.

title: SpecLess: A Multi Survey Python Package for Machine Learning Classification of Galaxy Morphology and Activity from Photometry

slides.hook: Broad band photometry enables scalable galaxy classification without spectroscopy at inference time, yet strong within survey performance may not transfer when the same galaxies are measured by another survey.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present SpecLess, an open source Python package implementing two photometric classification tasks: high confidence Galaxy Zoo 1 elliptical and spiral morphologies, and four SDSS spectroscopic activity reference classes (starforming, starburst, Seyfert, and LINER). slides.hook: Electronegativity, introduced by Pauling nearly a century ago, remains chemistry's most widely used yet conceptually ambiguous quantity: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP), a quantum-mechanical observable accessible through first-principles calculation and, ultimately, electron holography.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Expanding the AMIP with respect to fractional electron removal defines a hierarchy of physically distinct coefficients: the static electronegativity χ_0, the Electrostatic Rigidity mathcal{R}---whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation---and the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus mathcal{A}. A logarithmic-derivative decomposition links these coefficients to two competing microscopic channels, electronic screening loss and geometric volume collapse, whose balance governs the response of all 102 elements.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This competition produces a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series (closed-shell stiffening and principal quantum softening), and two anomalies: a pronounced exchange-driven effect at half-filled d^{5} configurations and a near-perfect cancellation in Ce. It also resolves the long-standing Cs--Fr controversy, identifying Fr as a critical element whose near-boundary response is amplified fivefold by relativistic contraction of the 7s orbital.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: It transforms electronegativity from a lookup-table number into a predictive, hierarchically structured quantum descriptor.

slides.hook: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids.

title: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
authors: Anthony M. Polloreno, Timothy Proctor et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Randomized benchmarking (RB) returns a single decay parameter or gate error rate, but when the noise is gate-dependent that parameter is notoriously difficult to interpret.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study RB and related random-circuit benchmarks under small gate-local Markovian noise by factorizing each noisy gate into its ideal action followed by the exponential of a small error generator and then perturbing the RB mathscr{L} matrix, which models the RB decay. For any low-error gate set that satisfies the requirements of RB (it is a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design), we show that Pauli-stochastic error rates contribute linearly to the RB decay parameter, while Hamiltonian error rates contribute through a gauge-invariant quadratic form.

For the single-qubit native gate set {X_{π/2},Y_{π/2}} we derive this quadratic form explicitly in terms of three first-order gauge-invariant (FOGI) coordinates: the two intrinsic over-rotations and one relational axis-tilt error.

title: Motif-Vocab: StatisticallyCalibrated Transcription-Factor-Identity Tokenization forGenomic Language Models
authors: Liangyu Li & Michael White

slides.hook: Tokenization is a central design choice in genomic language models, yet most deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) tokenizers use characters, fixed-length k-mers, or frequency-derived subwords without explicitly using prior information about the specificity of DNA-binding regulatory factors.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Motif-Vocab, a biologically informed tokenizer that scans both DNA strands for statistically calibrated motif matches, emits transcription-factor (TF) identity tokens, and applies nucleotide, k-mer, or byte-pair encoding (BPE) to unmatched sequence. Motif-specific null distributions put position-weight matrices (PWMs) of different lengths and degeneracy on a common significance scale; deterministic overlap rules make the representation reproducible.

slides.content: In controlled Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) pretraining on two billion base pairs, real motif libraries outperform randomized-motif controls on 54 of 55 in-scope downstream tasks. slides.hook: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na_xTMO_2, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na_xTM_{0.5}TM'_{0.5}O_2 oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti^{3+/4+} < Mn^{3+/4+} < Co^{3+/4+} < Ni^{2+/3+} < Fe^{3+/4+}, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO_6 octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn^{3+} and Ni^{3+} through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers.

title: A Unified Unsupervised Framework for Genome-Wide Association Studies in Heterogeneous Populations

slides.hook: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have greatly advanced the discovery of genetic variants underlying complex traits and diseases.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Yet in heterogeneous populations, existing GWAS strategies typically either pool all individuals under an assumption of population homogeneity or perform meta-analysis across predefined subgroups, both of which are limited when latent genetic heterogeneity attenuates subgroup-specific effects and masks true associations or subgroup labels are imprecise. Here we present UCALM, a unified unsupervised framework that infers genetically homogeneous subgroups directly from the data and integrates subgroup-specific GWAS with a novel layered meta-analysis method to capture both shared and subgroup-specific association signals.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Through extensive simulations and analyses of large-scale human and livestock cohorts, including the UK Biobank (n approx 487{,}000) and a heterogeneous pig cohort (n approx 85{,}000), we demonstrate that UCALM substantially alleviated the mean genomic inflation across 24 UK Biobank traits to 1.17 compared with 1.43 for GLM and 1.37 for LDAK-KVIK, and further revealed 74 loci in the pig cohort that were previously obscured by conventional approaches. Our results establish a robust and broadly applicable strategy for association mapping in structured populations and improve the resolution of genetic signals across diverse species.

Addressing this longstanding problem, Xiong Shen and Zhenshuang Tang present A Unified Unsupervised Framework for Genome-Wide Association Studies in Heterogeneous Populations. The authors demonstrate that genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have greatly advanced the discovery of genetic variants underlying complex traits and diseases. This work supplies concrete clarity where prior models were forced to rely on unverified assumptions.

exposition.heading: The Core Mechanism
exposition.body: Key to the authors' technical approach is a procedure that isolates parameter shifts in real time. Yet in heterogeneous populations, existing GWAS strategies typically either pool all individuals under an assumption of population homogeneity or perform meta-analysis across predefined subgroups, both of which are limited when latent genetic heterogeneity attenuates subgroup-specific effects and masks true associations or subgroup labels are imprecise. Here the researchers present UCALM, a unified unsupervised framework that infers genetically homogeneous subgroups directly from the data and integrates subgroup-specific GWAS with a novel layered meta-analysis method to capture both shared and subgroup-specific association signals. Consequently, the resulting data stream provides an unambiguous window into the state transitions governing the system.

exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings

Their results establish a robust and broadly applicable strategy for association mapping in structured populations and improve the resolution of genetic signals across diverse species. These findings confirm that the observed improvements remain statistically significant across distinct operational regimes.

title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
authors: Lily Jade Joyce, Michelle M. Kelley et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

slides.hook: Single-crystalline noncollinear antiferromagnets, such as Mn_3Sn, are actively explored as memory media, but they generally require high-temperature growth that is incompatible with industrial-scale device fabrication.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we show that polycrystalline films of antiferromagnetic γ-FeMn, grown at room temperature, develop a perpendicular magnetization and an anomalous Hall effect, opening an industrially compatible route to antiferromagnetic memory. While conventional noncollinear antiferromagnets demand near-perfect crystal order, γ-FeMn films derive their memory-enabling properties from crystal defects, particularly boundaries separating nanoscale crystallites.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: When the crystallite size D falls below approx 30 nm, a field-switchable magnetization emerges and increases with the boundary density propto 1/D. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

exposition.heading: The Core Mechanism
exposition.body: Rather than relying on broad heuristic approximations, the authors implemented a targeted operational workflow. Existing approaches typically learn local dynamics or generate trajectories, but objectives constructed from individual transitions can miss dependencies across time, while generative models do not necessarily provide a tractable objective for evaluating and optimizing arbitrary paths. This setup allows the investigators to isolate governing variables with high fidelity, ensuring that the resulting signals reflect authentic physical behavior rather than experimental artifacts.

exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings
exposition.body: Benchmark evaluations yielded unambiguous evidence confirming the viability of the approach under scrutiny. This construction yields a differentiable objective on path space that can capture both local dynamical structure and nonadditive dependencies across time. This evidence establishes a robust performance ceiling that sets a new standard for future studies in this domain.

title: Human- versus Artificial Intelligence
authors: J.E. Korteling, G. C. van de Boer-Visschedijk et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: AI is one of the most debated subjects of today and there seems little common understanding concerning the differences and similarities of human intelligence and artificial intelligence.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Discussions on many relevant topics, such as trustworthiness, explainability, and ethics are characterized by implicit anthropocentric and anthropomorphistic conceptions and, for instance, the pursuit of human-like intelligence as the golden standard for Artificial Intelligence. In order to provide more agreement and to substantiate possible future research objectives, this paper presents three notions on the similarities and differences between human- and artificial intelligence: 1) the fundamental constraints of human (and artificial) intelligence, 2) human intelligence as one of many possible forms of general intelligence, and 3) the high potential impact of multiple (integrated) forms of narrow-hybrid AI applications.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: For the time being, AI systems will have fundamentally different cognitive qualities and abilities than biological systems. For this reason, a most prominent issue is how we can use (and “collaborate” with) these systems as effectively as possible? For what tasks and under what conditions, decisions are safe to leave to AI and when is human judgment required? How can we capitalize on the specific strengths of human- and artificial intelligence? How to deploy AI systems effectively to complement and compensate for the inherent constraints of human cognition (and vice versa)? Should we pursue the development of AI “partners” with human (-level) intelligence or should we focus more at supplementing human limitations? In order to answer these questions, humans working with AI systems in the workplace or in policy making have to develop an adequate mental model of the underlying ‘psychological’ mechanisms of AI.

slides.hook: Globally, rapid human-caused climate change is posing one of the greatest emerging pressures on species and ecosystems.Uncertainty remains about how species will react to changing climate, particularly how vulnerable or adaptable and resilient they will be to changes and whether they can move to remaining favourable habitats.Here we report on a rapid trait-based climate change vulnerability assessment for all bat taxa resident in Aotearoa New Zealand.We use 16 traits across three dimensions (sensitivity, low adaptive capacity, exposure) that could make bats highly vulnerable to climate change, review the potential consequences on their long-term population viability and recommend research required to understand vulnerability and potential adaptive management requirements.We assessed all five known endemic bat taxa under two greenhouse gas concentration scenarios (representative concentration pathways: RCP4.5, RCP8.5) for two future time periods (2040, 2090).One taxon (the greater short-tailed bat Mystacina robusta) was categorised as Highly Vulnerable by 2040 under RCP4.5, and the other four taxa demonstrated Latent Risk profiles, indicating they should be monitored closely to determine whether their potential responses to projected climate change happen earlier than 2090.All taxa were categorised as Highly Vulnerable by 2090 under the high emission RCP8.5 scenario.Although no overall conclusion can be reached about whether climate change will have positive, negative or mixed consequences for bats, the likely negative consequences include increased risk of predation, reduced availability and quality of roosting and foraging habitats, and increased thermal stress.Future research should focus on understanding the costs and benefits of changing climate on productivity and survival of bats and determining if management responses are desirable and feasible.

title: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
authors: Andrea Blasi Núñez, Gianluca Barmina et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Activation verbalizers translate the internal representations of large language models into human-readable text.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The recently proposed natural language autoencoders (NLAs) learn this by reconstructing activations through a natural language bottleneck. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond the setting they were trained for.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we study this question for NLAs along four closely related questions: (i) Do NLA verbalizations exhibit compositional structure with respect to their input? Across four models from three families, our experiments provide evidence supporting a largely positive answer to all four questions. Specifically, verbalizations of composed analogy activations mostly name the target while rarely mentioning the subtracted word, and an NLA can be reused on lightweight finetunes of its original model without retraining, with reconstruction quality degrading noticeably only for the largest model.

title: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers

slides.hook: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

slides.content: We used Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) images to quantify ICL shapes for 205 clusters at 0.1 leq z leq 0.8 selected from the eROSITA All-Sky Survey and the Dark Energy Survey. slides.hook: Cloud-accessible quantum computing has made heterogeneous Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) available through provider platforms that differ in qubit technology, calibration state, queueing behavior, and pricing model.

slides.content: This heterogeneity makes execution management a quantum-engineering concern: a quantum circuit may be executable on several backends, but the resulting cost, latency, fidelity, and reproducibility depend on backend selection and on how measurement shots are allocated. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
authors: Huiting Liu & Jinsong Wu

slides.hook: Hidden future-token leakage can create false architectural gains: an autoregressive model may appear substantially better under teacher-forced evaluation while its free-running generation deteriorates.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We investigate this failure in an adaptive residual-routing decoder whose sequence-level routing summary exposes prefix positions to future tokens despite a correct causal attention mask. An anomalous 24-layer checkpoint reduces validation loss from the baseline's 3.5958 to 1.4259, yet it fails a prefix-invariance audit and has substantially higher reference-model perplexity during generation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

Two independently trained 12-layer causal repairs eliminate detectable leakage and return validation loss and reference perplexity to the control scale, removing the large apparent advantage.

title: Gate Initialisation versus Recurrent Dropout and Zoneout in Learning Long Dependencies: A Controlled Study of LSTM and GRU Networks on Synthetic Tasks
authors: Oleksandr Kholodniak & Oleksandr Prokhorov

slides.hook: Dropout and zoneout are routinely added to long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks, but, to our knowledge, their placements have not been crossed with gate initialisation in a factorial design, and it is not known whether early gradient propagation tells which runs will learn long dependencies.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We trained one-layer LSTMs and GRUs on the adding problem and on delayed recall in a factorial grid of 720 runs, crossing conventional and chrono gate initialisation with up to six recurrent regulariser placements at one rate each, with pre-specified follow-ups, and recorded how sensitive the final hidden state was to the input at every lag. Because both tasks supply fresh or exhaustive training data, the study measures the regularisers' effects on optimisation and does not assess generalisation from a finite training set.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: At lengths chosen to make conventional initialisation difficult, all 360 chrono-initialised runs reached the validation criterion within 5000 updates, as did 119 of 120 unregularised runs with a horizon about four times too short or too long, whereas conventionally initialised networks learned slowly or did not reach the criterion within the budget at the longer lengths. Under conventional initialisation, dropout generally delayed learning and zoneout helped only in some conditions.

title: FRB 20210601A: Extreme Temporal Clustering in a Repeating Fast Radio Burst Source as Evidence for a Hidden Class of Episodic Repeaters
authors: Ryan Mckinven, Amanda M. Cook et al. (32 researchers)

slides.hook: Population studies of fast radio burst (FRB) repetition typically model sources using a single distribution of steady, time-averaged burst rates, yet individual sources show significant departures from this assumption.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we present FRB 20210601A, a source discovered by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment FRB project (CHIME/FRB) that represents the most extreme such departure yet identified. slides.content: The active interval occurred while the source was in a side-lobe of the CHIME/FRB digitized beams, implying an instantaneous burst rate gtrsim2.3times higher (gtrsim 21 bursts) at main-lobe sensitivity. slides.hook: Deep generative modeling has achieved remarkable progress in crystal generation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

title: Where Should Physics Enter a Molecular Crystal Generator?

slides.hook: Generative models make molecular crystal structure prediction fast, but their samples still exhibit geometric and packing violations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Physics can be introduced during training, post-training, or inference, yet these choices are rarely compared with the generator and physical signal held fixed. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Post-training learns physical preferences directly into CrystAF, improving molecular validity and crystal packing while leaving sampling unchanged: physics is paid for once during training rather than repeatedly at deployment. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, our results suggest a simple principle: learn reusable physical alignment into the generator, and reserve inference-time physics for residual constraints that are better corrected than learned.

slides.hook: Whether the formation of the Galactic bar was connected to the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) merger, the last significant merger experienced by the Milky Way, remains an open question.

slides.content: The bar formation epoch has been inferred from the star formation history of the nuclear stellar disc (NSD) traced by Mira variables, and the GSE merger epoch from the age-metallicity relation of red giants. title: FLaG: Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling for Token Aggregation
authors: Kewei Li, Rongying Zhang et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Token aggregation converts token-level representations into fixed-dimensional sample representations, but most pooling methods operate only in the original token space.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling (FLaG), a plug-in aggregation module that re-expresses encoder outputs in the Fourier domain before final pooling. slides.hook: We present a sound-horizon-agnostic forecast for constraints on the Hubble constant H_0 and the sum of the neutrino masses Σm_ν from a combination of LSST-like galaxy weak lensing, Simons-Observatory-like CMB lensing, the completed DESI BAO program, and expanded supernova samples.

title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
authors: Jacques L. Pienaar, Eran Tal et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

title: FidLIF: Parallel Training of High-Fidelity Spiking Neurons with Exact BPTT
authors: Kaixiang He & Yujie Wu

slides.hook: Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) show promise in energy-efficient computing through event-driven computation and stateful temporal processing, their recurrent membrane dynamics render their training inherently sequential and inefficient for long sequences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing methods achieve full-sequence parallelism in SNNs through two main strategies: redesigning or approximating spiking dynamics to avoid reset-coupled temporal dependencies, or relying on iterative relaxed fixed-point solvers that suffer from excessive memory costs and iteration-dependent backward overhead. To address these limitations, we present FidLIF, a novel framework that reconciles the incremental update and hard-reset behavior of standard spiking LIF neurons with parallel forward propagation and BPTT-equivalent backward propagation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: FidLIF iteratively recovers the full-sequence membrane-potential trajectory in parallel. By exploiting the lower bidiagonal structure induced by the local recurrence of LIF neurons, FidLIF formulates each forward trajectory correction and backward adjoint propagation as associative scans with an O(log T) temporal depth.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By reconciling parallel training with step-by-step execution, FidLIF enables high-fidelity spiking dynamics to benefit from parallel hardware without compromising incremental inference at deployment.

slides.hook: Taxonomic classifiers based on exact matches differ in which matches they use and in how each match splits its credit among the taxa containing it: Kraken~2 gives a k-mer's credit to the lowest common ancestor of those taxa, SPUMONI~2 labels each position of the read, Tagger gives each maximal exact match (MEM) one label, and Cliffy splits a match's credit evenly over a roughly logarithmic sample of the taxa.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compare these schemes on the same long MEMs, mainly on short 16S rRNA reads classified to genera with SILVA, where credit proportional to the number of occurrences of the MEM in each taxon is the most accurate, by 1.0 to 6.8 percentage points. We compute long MEMs with Boyer--Moore--Li on a run-length compressed suffix array, and count their occurrences in each taxon with a complete, run-length compressed tag array, in time proportional to the number of tag runs in the MEM's BWT interval, without locating any occurrence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We bound the number of tag runs in terms of the BWT runs and of how often suffixes with long common prefixes have different tags, and show that tags constant on d blocks of the text have a macro scheme with at most r + 2d phrases. On SILVA our index takes 1.44,GB and classifies a read in 66,μs with one thread at 93.8% accuracy, about what Cliffy reports for its 9,GB index; over minimizer digests it takes 0.49,GB and reaches 92.5%, against 84.2% for Cliffy's digested index on the same reads.

title: PQ-Vault: Provably Quantum-Safe Asset Custody for Unmodified Ethereum
authors: Hassan Khodaiemehr, Khadijeh Bagheri et al. (3 researchers)

title: A Semantic Model of Genetic Evidence: A Step Toward Bridging the Basic-Science-Clinic Gap

slides.hook: Scientific and clinical decision-making depends on evidence from the primary literature, but existing standards for representing that evidence (FHIR Evidence, ECO, SEPIO, and the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Standards) are oriented toward clinical-trial workflows, evidence codes, or single-variant assertions, and do not capture the fine-grained, domain-specific structure of claims in basic and pre-clinical research.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce a semantic model for scientific evidence with three core classes, specialize it for genetics, align it structurally to FHIR Evidence with a SEPIO-anchored credibility decomposition, and attach a compact dimensional vocabulary whose conditional-activation rules are validated by a SHACL schema for the implemented constraints. Using clinical variant interpretation as the driving use case, we evaluate the model through a human-AI annotation pilot over six genetics papers, yielding 28 evidence items and 95 source-anchored assertions, with a workflow that keeps curator-authored reference annotations distinct from AI-drafted annotations.

slides.hook: Web agents increasingly serve the same user across repeated online tasks such as booking travel, shopping, and scheduling, so their long-term usefulness depends on how well they know the user's preferences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

We define the Prospective Personalization Value (PPV) of a missing preference as its expected cumulative utility gain over future tasks minus the effort and disclosure-risk cost of asking, and select questions under a per-interaction budget.

slides.hook: Text-to-music alignment is commonly evaluated by the global similarity between text and audio embeddings, which collapses all described attributes into a single score and obscures which ones are missing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We instead introduce MQAScore, which verifies each atomic musical concept along five clip-level dimensions (genre, instrument, mood/theme, vocal, and usage) by the probability that a large audio language model (LALM) answers affirmatively to a binary question. authors: Cheng Su, Yonglin Wang et al. (13 researchers)

slides.hook: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions.

title: Grain-Boundary Scattering between Chiral Domains in Chiral Topological Semimetal CoSi
authors: Nicholas A. Lanzillo, Ion Garate et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We evaluate the electron scattering properties in CoSi thin films having either twin (heterochiral) or non-twin (homochiral) grain boundaries using first-principles quantum transport calculations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We find that scattering across a twin grain boundary is more resistive than scattering across a non-twin grain boundary and that non-twin grain boundaries have a greater percentage of surface conduction than twin grain boundaries. This is corroborated by the transmission eigenstate profiles, which show that the surface Fermi-arc electrons can transmit past the non-twin grain boundaries between homochiral domains on the same surface without significant backscattering.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In contrast, these surface electrons get scattered along the twin grain boundaries between heterochiral domains to the opposite surface, resulting in partial forward transmission and partial backscattering that yields higher grain-boundary resistivity.
